title: Hybrid SLC-MLC RRAM Mixed-Signal Processing-in-Memory Architecture for Transformer Acceleration via Gradient Redistribution
problem: Analog RRAM PIM using multi-level cells (MLC) can offer 2x storage density and higher compute throughput than single-level cells (SLC), but MLC's non-linearity causes catastrophic accuracy degradation (e.g., 40% drop) in Transformer models, while brute-force hybrid SLC/MLC mapping fails to move enough weights into MLC to yield meaningful efficiency gains.
motivation: Transformers dominate inference workloads and are memory-bandwidth-limited; analog RRAM PIM can eliminate data movement and exploit massive parallelism, but accuracy sensitivity to MLC non-ideality has blocked analog PIM from covering the dominant fraction of transformer weights.
method: HyFlexPIM uses a three-tier mixed-signal RRAM PIM architecture: (1) digital SLC RRAM PIM for attention Q·K^T and ×V operations that require high precision and write real-time vectors, (2) analog SLC RRAM PIM for the most critical static weight rows, and (3) analog MLC RRAM PIM (2-bit per cell) for the error-tolerant majority of static weights. A single analog PIM module is reconfigurable between SLC and MLC via a shared 6-b/7-b flexible SAR-ADC that bypasses the MSB comparison in SLC mode, adding less than 1% area/energy overhead. On the software side, gradient redistribution applies SVD to decompose each linear weight matrix, truncates to a hard threshold rank to maintain iso-computational cost, then fine-tunes for 1-3 epochs with AdamW; the fine-tuning process naturally concentrates gradient magnitude into the top 5-10% of singular values, making those rows clearly demarcated as SLC-critical while 90-95% of weights are safely mapped to MLC.
key_novelty: Gradient redistribution via SVD truncation followed by fine-tuning actively reshapes gradient distributions to concentrate critical weight importance into 5-10% of parameters, enabling 90-95% of Transformer weights to be computed in efficient MLC RRAM while preserving less than 1% accuracy loss.
contributions: Reconfigurable hybrid SLC-MLC analog RRAM PIM module with a shared flexible 6-b/7-b SAR-ADC (<1% area/energy overhead for dual-mode support)
Three-tier mixed-signal architecture: digital RRAM PIM for attention, analog SLC for critical weights, analog MLC for error-tolerant majority
SVD-based gradient redistribution algorithm that concentrates 90-95% of Transformer weights into MLC-compatible low-gradient ranks through post-truncation fine-tuning
Maximum 1.86x throughput and 1.45x energy efficiency improvement over state-of-the-art with <1% accuracy degradation across BERT, GPT-2, Llama3, and ViT-Base

metrics.speedup: 1.86x max throughput over ASADI (SoA analog-digital hybrid PIM)
metrics.area: 65nm technology node; <1% area overhead for SLC/MLC reconfigurability
metrics.accuracy: <1% accuracy degradation for encoder (BERT) and vision (ViT); <10% loss increase for decoder (GPT-2, Llama3)
metrics.other: 5-10% SLC protection rate sufficient for encoders; 5-20% for decoders

baselines: ASADI (FP32 analog-digital hybrid PIM, SLC only)
SPRINT (digital processor + analog PIM for attention only)
limitations: HyFlexPIM is optimized for inference only; the SVD fine-tuning step incurs a one-time preprocessing cost not counted in inference latency, and the 65nm process node used for comparison may not reflect leading-edge RRAM process feasibility.
primary_theme: Hybrid SLC-MLC RRAM PIM with gradient redistribution for transformer inference
